ei.intro: Endpoint-independent NAT44 (VPP nat44-ei): one outside port per inside endpoint whatever the destination, so any remote host can reach a mapped inside endpoint (full-cone behaviour). It uses the same NAT44 settings as ED — Outbound, Static & port forwards and Pools — without twice-NAT and load-balanced mappings. ED and EI are mutually exclusive.
ei.modeEi: NAT44 runs in EI mode: the Outbound, Static and Pools tabs are applied with nat44-ei.
ei.modeEd: NAT44 runs in ED mode. Switch to EI to apply the NAT44 settings with nat44-ei (twice-NAT and load-balanced mappings must be removed first).

sessions.truncated: counts stopped at the agent's scan limit
sessions.manualRefresh: refreshed by hand (a filter makes the agent scan sessions)

kill.title: Delete NAT44-EI session?
kill.question: The session is removed from the data plane; the host opens a new one with its next packet.

nat64.intro: Stateful NAT64 (RFC 6146): IPv6-only clients reach IPv4 hosts through the NAT64 prefix (default 64:ff9b::/96), translated to the IPv4 pool. Clients need DNS64 (RFC 6147) to learn the synthesized addresses. This is also the provider side (PLAT) of 464XLAT.

nat66.intro: NAT66: stateless 1:1 translation of one IPv6 address to another between the inside and outside interfaces (VPP nat66).

nptv6.intro: NPTv6 (RFC 6296): stateless, checksum-neutral translation of an internal IPv6 prefix to an external one on an interface. One binding per interface; both prefixes have the same length, at most /64.
nptv6.writeOnlyHelp: VPP cannot list NPTv6 bindings: the agent applies every binding of the running configuration and re-applies it on each resync, but cannot read it back.

prefix.title: NAT64 prefix
prefix.help: RFC 6052 length 32/40/48/56/64/96; 64:ff9b::/96 is the well-known prefix
